extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, national patent offices, examiners, and policymakers operating under the Eurasian Patent Convention
extracted.subtask_description: Official regional treaty text setting substantive and procedural rules for obtaining, maintaining and enforcing Eurasian patents, including patentability criteria, filing/examination procedures, fees, publication, conversion to national applications and institutional governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office shall grant a Eurasian patent for any invention that is new, involves an inventive step and is industrially applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to a Eurasian patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to a Eurasian patent shall belong to the inventor or his successor in title; where the inventor is an employee, entitlement is determined in accordance with the law of the State in which the employee is mainly employed (or, if not determinable, the law of the State where the employer has a place of business to which the employee is attached). For proceedings before the Eurasian Office, the applicant shall be deemed to be entitled to the Eurasian patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of priority shall be recognized in conformity with the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive patent rights and provisional protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a Eurasian patent shall have the exclusive right to use, and to authorize use or prohibit others from using, the patented invention; the owner may assign or license his rights. After publication of an application, the applicant shall enjoy provisional protection in conformity with national legislation of the Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of legal protection determined by claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the legal protection conferred by a Eurasian patent shall be determined by the claims. The description and drawings shall serve only to interpret the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of Eurasian patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a Eurasian patent shall be 20 years from the filing date of the Eurasian application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licenses for the use of a Eurasian patent by third parties may be granted in conformity with the Paris Convention by the competent authority of a Contracting State with effect in the territory of that State; such decisions may be contested in the courts or other competent authorities of that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity and enforcement handled by national authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Disputes concerning validity or infringement of a Eurasian patent in a given Contracting State shall be resolved by that State's national courts or other competent authorities on the basis of this Convention and the Patent Regulations; decisions have effect only in the territory of that State. National courts shall provide the same civil or other liability as for national patents and may require translations of the Eurasian patent into the State language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of criteria of patentability and disclosure requirement (Patent Regulations substantive provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide for the definition of the criteria of patentability of an invention, including the definition of novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, and the requirement of the disclosure of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures that do not affect patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall specify disclosures that do not affect the patentability of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide for the requirement of unity of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effects of right of priority (Patent Regulations item)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall define the right of priority and its effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the exclusive right in the patented invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall define the exclusive right conferred by the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of the prior user
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall address the right of the prior user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide for the interpretation of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of the inventor to be mentioned
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide for the right of the inventor to be mentioned in the Eurasian application and Eurasian patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and transfer of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide for the assignment and other transfer of the right to a Eurasian application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality in processing Eurasian applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide for confidentiality in processing Eurasian applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels and effect of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A Eurasian application may be filed with the Eurasian Office or (for applicants from a Contracting State where provided by national law) through that State's national Office. An application filed through a national Office has the same effect as if filed with the Eurasian Office, provided it is transmitted within time limits prescribed by the Patent Regulations. The national Office verifies compliance as to form before transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary procedural fee and national transmittal fee rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where filed with the Eurasian Office, a unitary procedural fee for filing, search, publication and other processing is payable at filing; where filed through a national Office, a fee is payable to the national Office for examination as to form and transmittal, and the unitary procedural fee is payable to the Eurasian Office upon transmittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination as to form and search by the Eurasian Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office shall verify compliance with requirements as to form and shall carry out a search in relation to the Eurasian application. The search shall result in a search report which shall be forwarded to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and early publication option
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office shall publish the Eurasian application together with the search report promptly after the expiry of 18 months from the filing date or, where priority is claimed, from the priority date. At the request of the applicant the Eurasian Office shall publish the Eurasian application earlier; in that case the search report will be published separately as soon as it is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination and fee/timing
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the applicant, to be filed with the Eurasian Office before the expiry of six months from the date of publication of the search report, the Eurasian Office shall carry out substantive examination of the application; filing that request is subject to payment of an examination fee to the Eurasian Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant or reject by collegia of three examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to grant a Eurasian patent or reject the application shall be made by collegia composed of three examiners each, who shall be staff members of the Eurasian Office and, unless otherwise decided by unanimous Administrative Council decision, nationals of different Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal against refusal — time limit, composition and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant disagrees with a refusal, he may, within three months following receipt of the notice of refusal, lodge an appeal with the Eurasian Office which shall be examined by a collegium composed in conformity with the grant collegia; the appeal collegium shall include at least two examiners who did not participate in the original decision. Lodging the appeal is subject to payment of a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for grant and payment timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of a Eurasian patent shall be subject to the payment of a fee to the Eurasian Office within three months after the date on which the applicant receives notice from the Eurasian Office that it is ready to grant the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of grant across Contracting States from publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the provisions of Article 17 (maintenance/designation), a Eurasian patent shall have effect on the territory of all Contracting States from the date of its publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the Eurasian Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person entitled to be a representative before a national Office and registered with the Eurasian Office as a patent agent may act as representative before the Eurasian Office. Applicants without residence or principal place of business in any Contracting State must be represented by such a patent agent. Persons resident or having principal place of business in a Contracting State may act personally or via agents/representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of Eurasian applications into national applications after refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the expiry of six months from the date on which the applicant receives notice of the Eurasian Office’s refusal to grant or refusal to allow an appeal, the applicant may request designation of Contracting States in which he wishes to obtain national patents; the Eurasian application shall then be treated in each designated State as a regular national application with the same filing and priority dates and further processed by the national Office upon payment of prescribed national fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees and designation for continuing effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance of a Eurasian patent requires annual payment of fees in each year following grant, payable by the date corresponding to the filing date. Continuing effect of the patent in each Contracting State requires the owner to designate by name each Contracting State in which effect is to continue; such designation is addressed to the Eurasian Office and made at the same time as payment of the maintenance fee, which is payable with respect to each designated Contracting State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: ownership, distribution and state-specific amounts/currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees concerning any Eurasian application or patent and charges for services are payable to the Eurasian Office and (subject to paragraph 2) belong to the Organization. The examination-as-to-form/transmittal fee (Article 15(2)) is payable to and belongs to the national Office with which filed. All maintenance fees are payable to the Eurasian Office; distribution ratio between the Organization and designated Contracting States is fixed by Administrative Council (with at least one-fifth belonging to the Organization). The amount of maintenance fees for each Contracting State is fixed by that State; the Administrative Council determines the currency for payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Regulations — procedural provisions (detailed list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Regulations shall provide for details concerning Eurasian patent procedure, in particular: (i) requirements as to form and contents of the application; (ii) patent agents, certification and registration procedures; (iii) the filing date; (iv) calculation of time limits; (v) claiming of priority; (vi) currencies and procedures for payment of fees; (vii) amendment or correction of the application; (viii) patent search and examination; (ix) documentation and information services by the Eurasian Office; (x) publication of applications and patents; (xi) the Register of Eurasian Patents; (xii) the Gazette of the Eurasian Office; (xiii) conditions and procedures for administrative revocation of patents; (xiv) conversion of applications into national applications; (xv) application of provisions where multiple inventors/applicants/owners/representatives exist; (xvi) contacts of the Office with applicants/patent owners/agents and procedures for consultation of files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Cooperation Treaty and its Regulations shall be applied in the Eurasian Patent System; in case of conflict the PCT prevails. The Eurasian Office shall be a receiving Office and also a designated and an elected Office under the PCT and may apply for status as an International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authority with Administrative Council authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional search and collegia arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Office may, with Administrative Council authorization, conclude agreements with national or regional patent offices for carrying out searches of the same type as under the PCT. For as long as necessary, collegia of three examiners may also consist of examiners recommended by national Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of national patent systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The Convention does not prejudice the right of any Contracting State to grant national patents and does not prevent any State from participating independently in other international organizations or developing other forms of international cooperation in industrial property protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of the Convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Convention may be revised at any time by the Contracting States; the Administrative Council decides on convocation of revision conferences and the rules/procedures of such conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement of disputes via WIPO mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a dispute arises concerning interpretation or implementation of the Convention, the Director General of WIPO shall, at the request of any party to the dispute, mediate to lead parties to settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of patent information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting State shall receive, free of charge, the Gazette of the Eurasian Office and the descriptions of Eurasian applications and patents. Subject to this, no publication of the Eurasian Office may be disseminated free of charge without Administrative Council authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for signature, accession and entry into force
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State that is a member of the United Nations and bound by the Paris Convention and the Patent Cooperation Treaty may become party to this Convention by signature and ratification or by accession. No reservations are permitted. The Convention enters into force three months after required instruments of ratification/accession are deposited (special rule for first three States).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State may denounce the Convention by notification to the Director General of WIPO; denunciation takes effect six months after receipt of the notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General of WIPO shall be the depositary of the Convention.
